messages:
inc-bot: anomalous increase in 5xx + gateway timeouts for /v1/generate in us-west-2 over last 4m — rolling alert threshold hit :warning:

pagerbot: P-2347 created and paging @oncall-ml. Acknowledge to stop paging.

Priya: I'm seeing alerts too. Error budget burn rate spiking. Notified support.

oncall-ml: acknowledged, pulling up logs and process lists. Initial glance: multiple model-runner workers exiting unexpectedly with 'Killed' and 'segfault' messages. Checking container runtime and OOM events.

Dev: which runner image is in prod? We had a perf change earlier to enable the vectorized attention fast-path.

Ravi: prod image: model-runner:2026-04-02-fastattn. Canary looked fine but rollout finished ~90m ago.

oncall-ml: gathering `dmesg` and kube events...

oncall-ml: paste logs: ````
Apr 02 09:43:21 runner-07 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (model-runner) score 987 or sacrifice child
Apr 02 09:43:22 runner-07 model-runner[4123]: terminated by signal 9 (SIGKILL)
Apr 02 09:43:23 runner-07 kernel: model-runner[4129]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f4a5678ef12 sp 00007ffda3e1e8e0
````

oncall-ml: core dumps present on a few nodes: `/var/lib/systemd/coredump/core.model-runner.*`. Getting a backtrace now.

Tess: I'm throttling noisy tenants at the edge and turning off speculative prefetch for embeddings to reduce memory churn.

Liam: I've staged a traffic-split to steer >50% of high-throughput customers to a CPU-served fallback (redwood/text-compact-2025) while we stabilize. This will reduce quality but keep latency and availability. Live in ~90s.

oncall-ml: mitigation checklist I'm applying: 1) pause rollout of 2026-04-02-fastattn 2) scale up spare pool in us-east-1 for critical tenant failover 3) set env `USE_FASTATTN=false` on affected daemonset 4) reduce max batch tokens to 256 5) drain & recreate nodes that show kernel OOMs.

Dev: note: fast-attention uses handwritten SIMD kernels — there's a known potential misalignment on some CPU micro-architectures that could cause crashes under particular token lengths. Could be related.

oncall-ml: running `gdb` on core from runner-07:````
#0  0x00007f4a5678ef12 in simd_attention_compute(unsigned char*, unsigned long)
#1  0x00007f4a5656abcd in forward_layer
#2  0x00005555556ff123 in serve_request
````

oncall-ml: stacktrace points to simd_attention_compute — consistent with vectorized kernel.

Priya: OK, we need both short-term mitigation and a patch plan. Short-term: roll back image and disable fast path. Medium-term: add runtime guard to fall back to safe kernel when mem_errs or crashes detected. Long-term: add hardware/cpu-variant matrix for fast-path enablement.

Ravi: rolling back daemonset for nodepool `usw2-inference-1` to model-runner:2026-03-29-stable. Starting now, ETA ~7m.

Tess: disabling speculative prefetch conf change applied to the platform and rate limits at API gateway increased enforcement for bursty orgs.

oncall-ml: after applying `USE_FASTATTN=false` on one node and lowering batch, I repro'd lower memory footprint locally. Pushing change cluster-wide in a controlled manner.

inc-bot: rollback job initiated id=rb-5873, targets 10 nodes in usw2.

Dev: I also recommend adding an emergency runtime flag that causes any segmentation fault within model-runner to be caught and the process to exit with 503 rather than crashing the whole pod (sandbox the kernel-call). Can we land that in a hotfix?

oncall-ml: agreement: treat crash as degradation — we can introduce a top-level signal handler to convert faults into error responses where feasible. Alex/Dev to follow up in hotfix.

Liam: failover routing for top 20 tenants is live to us-east spare pool. Notifying account owners.

Ravi: rollback completed on 10/10 nodes at 1782001498. A few nodes required reboots to clear oom-kill state.

oncall-ml: monitoring: error rate for /v1/generate in usw2 dropped from 22% -> 3% after rollback. Gateway timeouts have reduced.

Priya: capturing customer impact: ~30 orgs experienced transient 5xx during a 40-minute window; highest-impact tenants were moved to spare pool with near-zero downtime. No request body data lost. Support is drafting outbound comms.

Tess: uploading logs, core dumps, and node snapshots to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/P-2347/ (logs.tar.gz, cores/, snapshots/).

oncall-ml: I'll stay on to run further validations for 30m. Handoff: @Priya will own postmortem + customer comms.

Priya: taking ownership. Action items I'll track: - postmortem timeline - hotfix to disable fastattn by default & runtime signal handling - add rollout canary across more instance types - add automatic rollback trigger (5xx>8% for 5m) - add mem-pressure metrics alerting threshold.

Dev: creating hotfix branch now and will push a PR referencing P-2347. Will include unit test for alignment and a CI job to run against multiple CPU vendor images.

Liam: support update sent to impacted accounts; most reply acknowledging. Will keep a watch for escalations.

Priya: preliminary incident summary: duration ~42 minutes, root cause = vectorized attention fast-path causing crashes / memory pressure on some host types under certain sequence lengths -> widespread 5xx. Remediated via rollback + disabling fast-path + traffic failover. Postmortem to follow.

Ravi: closing pager. We'll keep monitoring for 24h.

oncall-ml: final note: saved one affected node as forensic preserve (do not reprovision) and collected kernel + perf captures. Will attach to postmortem.

Priya: thanks all, good mitigation. :clap:

inc-bot: incident P-2347 status set to mitigated at 1782001859
